osm_reviews.name: 名羽線跡
evidence: Suzuki Shoten Memorial Museum's Akebono archive states that the Meiu railway's Akebono–Sankebetsu section opened in 1962, allowing direct coal transport from the Haboro and Kamihaboro pits to Chikubetsu.

Haboro Tourism Association's 2019 coal-mine guide records completion of the 3.9 km Akebono–Sankebetsu section in December 1962 and the Haboro mine/railway closure in 1970. Its timeline distinguishes this working section from Meiu construction being frozen in 1981.
osm_reviews.geometry_assessment: The OSM feature runs southeast from immediately south of former Akebono station to the Sankebetsu/Haboro mine area. It is the coal-working corridor, rather than the remote never-opened Shumarinai continuation.
limits: This evidence confirms industrial operation of the corridor, not public passenger service.
The exact historical end of the working track was not independently surveyed. Preserve OSM remnant geometry with its source-quality caveat; do not claim survey precision or add missing connections.
No exact opening or closing day is assigned.

osm_reviews.evidence: Hakodate city's response describes Toi railway construction being stopped, with former construction land later reused as a walking route. It was not a former operating railway.

hokkaido_supplement_clarification.decision: Full mixed KML path conservatively excluded; frozen Hokkaido supplement unchanged.
hokkaido_supplement_clarification.reason: The KML path includes the industrially operated Akebono–Sankebetsu beginning AND a long never-opened continuation. The exclusion must not be described as proving the entire path never carried trains. OSM w990215687 supplies the retained coal-working remnant.
